title: autotune: sensible batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce autotuned defaults for batching and prefix caching, add quantization profile presets and a unit-economics dashboard + CLI to estimate cost improvements. Backwards compatible; can be toggled per-model.
description:
Summary: This change adds an autotune pipeline and sensible defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, ships a set of tested quantization profile presets, and introduces a lightweight unit-economics tool (console + CLI) to estimate per-token cost savings for a given workload. Motivation: Teams repeatedly pick suboptimal batching/cache settings and quantization profiles; manual tuning is slow and error-prone. This PR gives good defaults, an automated suggestion flow, and visibility into unit economics so developers can make informed tradeoffs.

What I changed (single-line sections):
- runtime: add "autotune" pipeline that collects sequence length distributions and cold-start latency signals then computes recommended target_batch_ms, max_batch_tokens, and prefix cache TTL per-route; integrates with existing serving config and feature gates; defaults are conservative and opt-in via route config.
- caching: default prefix/KV cache TTL heuristics and size limits; add cache warmup hinting for common prefixes.
- batching: new default target latency percentile (p95 target) based batching mode and per-model profiles to avoid pathological batching on short sequences.
- quantization: add three curated quant-profiles (safe, balanced, aggressive) with metadata (expected token-quality delta, throughput gain, supported hardware). Profiles are small JSON presets that map to compile-time flags.
- tooling: unit-econ CLI (redwood optimize unit-econ) and console dashboard with per-route cost delta previews; includes example workloads and quick-start.
- docs/tests: updated quickstart, new autotune guide, and end-to-end integration tests.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc (linked in Linear ENG-4123)
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] console dashboard wireup
- [x] docs and examples
- [x] feature gate and canary rollout plan

Commits summary:
- feat(autotune): collect seqlen distribution + latency signals and initial suggester
- feat(runtime): plumb recommendations into route config with safe defaults and feature flag
- feat(quant): add quant profiles (safe/balanced/aggressive) + mapping to model compile flags
- feat(tooling): add unit-econ CLI + console endpoints + sample workloads
- refactor(cache): heuristics for prefix TTL + warmup hints
- test: add integration tests for batching + cache + quantization combos
- docs: autotune guide + CLI usage + examples

Files changed (high-level):
- redwood/runtime/autotune.py (new)
- redwood/runtime/batching.py (tuning + new enum for p95_target_mode)
- redwood/runtime/cache.py (TTL heuristics + warmup hints)
- redwood/optimize/quant_profiles.json (new presets)
- redwood/console/unit_econ.py (dashboard endpoints)
- tools/cli/unit_econ.py (CLI)
- docs/autotune.md, docs/quantization.md, docs/unit-econ.md
- tests/integration/test_autotune_flow.py
- examples/autotune/sample_workload.json

Small patch example (illustrative):
- in redwood/runtime/batching.py updated default: target_batch_ms = 8 -> 5 for short-seq profiles
- in redwood/optimize/quant_profiles.json added "balanced" profile: {"bits":8, "kv_compression": "fp16-friendly", "expected_quality_delta": "~0.5%"}

Rollout plan:
- feature gate = autotune.recommendations (off by default)
- step 1: enable for internal canary (5% traffic) and run unit-econ estimation across two weeks
- step 2: expose suggestions in console for users to opt-in per-route
- step 3: enable auto-apply for Dedicated reserved pools where customer opts in via policy

Validation:
- integration tests assert stable latency (p95) while reducing tokens/second cost by >= 10% on benchmark corpora for recommended profiles
- e2e tests cover quant profile selection + fallback to safe profile on incompatibility

Monitoring and rollback:
- metrics added: autotune.suggestions.count, autotune.apply.success, autotune.rollback.count, unit_econ.estimated_savings_usd
- alert if p95 latency increases > 20% post-apply for 5 minutes across 3 hosts -> automatic rollback of that route

Notes for reviewers:
- I kept the defaults conservative; the heavy tuning lives in profiles and our autotune suggester. Please focus review on safety boundaries (cache TTL upper bounds, quant profile compatibility table) and the unit-econ math.
- The CLI accepts a small sample workload and outputs estimated per-token cost delta and projected monthly $ savings.

Related work: Linear ENG-4123, ENG-4180. SUP-321 was the customer report that motivated prefix cache heuristics.

Merge: squash and merge after approvals and green CI.

review_comments: Samir Gupta: Overall looks good; can we add a hard upper bound to cache TTL to avoid memory blowups in dedicated pools?
Asha Patel: Added ttl_max per-pool and documented defaults. Also added a unit test to assert upper bound enforcement.
Lena Wong: Quant profiles look reasonable - please add a short note on expectedquality vs throughput tradeoffs in docs.
Asha Patel: Added the tradeoff table to docs/quantization.md and included expected throughput numbers from microbenchmarks.
Tomoko Sato: CLI UX looks good; suggest printing a short explanation if sample workload is too small for reliable estimates.
Asha Patel: Added a min-sample warning and fallbacks to historical defaults.
notes_for_ops: When enabling auto-apply for Dedicated pools, ensure unit_econ telemetry is enabled for that customer ID. Ops should watch autotune.apply.success and unit_econ.estimated_savings_usd during rollout.
backcompat_notes: Backwards compatible. Autotune suggestions are off by default and stored separately from route configs until explicitly applied. Quant profiles are additive; unsafe aggressive profile requires explicit opt-in.
testing_instructions: Run pytest tests/integration/test_autotune_flow.py with sample_workload.json; use tools/cli/unit_econ.py --sample examples/autotune/sample_workload.json to reproduce unit-econ output. Follow docs/autotune.md for local canary run instructions.
